# [CS067] Infrastructure Type Crosses Layer Boundary (arch-boundary-type-leak)

A layer's exported API exposes types of a layer it should hide.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Architecture |
| **CWE** | - |
| **OWASP** | - |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

When a service method returns *sql.Rows or a gorm model, callers depend on the storage technology through it. Return domain types instead.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
func (s *UserService) Find(ctx context.Context, id int64) (*sql.Row, error)
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
func (s *UserService) Find(ctx context.Context, id int64) (domain.User, error)
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [arch-boundary-type-leak]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    arch-boundary-type-leak: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore arch-boundary-type-leak -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** arch-boundary-type-leak
```
